text:
maya: FYI ACME reported a big p99 jump ~3x starting ~11:30 UTC, customer saw timeouts and auth retries. They say errors spike when model=redwood-13b-q4 at higher concurrency.

josh: do we have OOMs on the node? which pool?

maya: logs show GPU OOMs and high KV memory usage on pool:dense-us-east-1. Node gpu-az1-07 had repeated allocator failures: 
```
runtime: allocation failed: failed to grab slab for 128MB chunk
kv_cache.size=85GB kv_slots=524k
OOM at 2024-06-12T11:34:12Z
```

priya: looks like KV growth + fragmentation. Any recent rollout that increased prefix caching or switched model variant?

maya: customer increased batch_size from 2->4, and we rolled a new quantized kernel last night to that shard.

amanda: @infra-oncall can you pull the slab heatmap and allocator stats for gpu-az1-07? need p95/p99 allocation latencies.

infra-oncall: pulling now. quick summary: slab utilization 93%, free segments are highly fragmented (lots of small holes), p99 alloc latency 120ms (baseline 12ms). KV cache high-water 86GB, evictions spike at same time.

support-bot: Incident note created: INC-2024-1832 linked to thread 1748123456.

josh: root cause hypothesis: combined effect of larger batches + kernel change causing slightly larger per-request KV pressure, pushing slab to fragmentation and forcing slow coalesces. Leads to alloc stalls -> increased CPU scheduling -> p99 latency.

priya: mitigation plan (short):
- immediate: throttle batch size for the tenant to 2, enable active fallback routing to lower-capacity model variant (redwood-13b-q4-lite) for that account.
- short term: restart kv-manager on gpu-az1-07 with warmup disabled to force compact path.
- medium: bump allocator compaction aggressiveness and reduce MALLOC_ARENA_MAX equivalent in our allocator config.

amanda: can we do the restart without tenant impact?

infra-oncall: yes, we can drain requests off gpu-az1-07 and roll restart of kv-manager; estimate ~90s disruption if we route traffic away first. I'll coordinate.

maya: repro checklist for post-mitigation validation:
1) repro load: run the customer prompt mix with concurrency 20 and batch_size 4 for 10 minutes (use run-repro.sh).
2) verify no OOMs in journalctl and no alloc p99 > 40ms.
3) check KV cache size trend and eviction rate.
4) confirm p95/p99 return to baseline within 30 minutes.

josh: run these commands on node (for infra):
```bash
# heatmap export
curl -sS http://localhost:9100/debug/allocator/heatmap > /tmp/heatmap.json
# alloc stats
curl -sS http://localhost:9100/debug/allocator/stats | jq '.'
# tail runtime logs
journalctl -u redwood-kv -n 200 -o short-monotonic
```

priya: allocator knobs we should try if restart not enough: 
- compaction.threshold := 0.6 (was 0.8)
- compaction.interval := 30s (was 120s)
- eviction.batch_limit := 1024 (was 4096)
- kv-prefetch.enabled := false for affected pool

amanda: also try immediate customer-side mitigations: reduce their max_concurrency or set request_concurrency=1 for large prompting flows. That buys time.

infra-oncall: actioning now: draining gpu-az1-07, enabling fallback routing for tenant acme-123, and scheduling kv-manager restart. ETA 5m.

maya: noted. I'll message customer and ask them to hold large batch runs until we confirm.

support-bot: [automated] fallback routing enabled for tenant acme-123 -> redwood-13b-q4-lite at 2024-06-12T11:40:05Z.

(5m later)

infra-oncall: drain complete, restart started. kv-manager restarted, warmup disabled. running quick health checks.

josh: after restart what does the slab heatmap look like?

infra-oncall: heatmap shows larger contiguous free segments, slab utilization down to 78%, p99 alloc latency dropped to 18ms in first 2 mins. KV cache down to 60GB after eviction wave.

priya: good. start repro load and monitor p95/p99.

maya: running repro now against the node. initial p99 at warmup ~85ms but trending down.

(10m later)

maya: repro finished. p95 back to baseline, p99 ~30ms (still slightly above baseline). No OOMs. eviction rate normalized.

josh: follow-ups:
- infra to tweak compaction.threshold and compaction.interval next deployment if fragmentation recurs (owner: infra team).
- runtime to add automatic adaptive eviction when KV hit >80% for pool (owner: runtime).
- support to keep customer on soft throttle for 24h and re-evaluate.

amanda: i'll send ANS to customer with summary and ask them to postpone batch_size changes until we've shipped allocator tuning.

maya: assigning owners: infra-oncall -> infra (postmortem + config change PR), josh -> runtime (adaptive eviction RFC), amanda -> customer comms, priya -> validation run tomorrow.

support-bot: Incident INC-2024-1832 updated: mitigations applied, monitoring healthy.

maya: thanks all :thumbsup:
